rationale: Evaluating omission of required braking requires characterising both whether braking is needed and whether it occurs. H-1 and FR-7 establish collision-avoiding braking as the relevant vehicle response; H-1’s failure to stop in time and FR-7.1’s braking-initiation requirement support including timeliness. P remains focused on this braking behaviour in the supplied hazardous situation, without incorporating the internal sensing, computation, communication, or control mechanisms that enable it.
determining_elements: “Whether a braking maneuver is required” identifies the condition necessary to evaluate omission under SG-1.
“Whether braking is actually initiated in time to avoid collision” characterises the required behaviour itself, supported by H-1, FR-7, and FR-7.1.
The operational scope reproduces H-1’s straight-ahead, 50 km/h, good-weather pedestrian-crossing situation.
The scoped “braking/avoidance response” is tied to collision-avoiding braking, which the target and FR-7 establish as part of the phenomenon.
